name: SHACKLETON RIM — steep uphill on the polar rim

meta.site: Shackleton Crater rim — lunar south pole
meta.citation: NASA LRO LOLA polar GDR, south of 87.5 S, 5 m/px
meta.grid: azimuthal equidistant about the site, resampled bilinear, long axis on bearing 103 deg
meta.resolution_note: source product is 5 m/px; this 1024x512 grid at 1.25 m/px spans 256 x 128 source posts and is a 4x bilinear resampling of them — interpolation, not added detail
meta.layout: row-major, +x along the traverse, +y to its left
meta.note: Steep rim ascent. Best public lunar topography anywhere: 5 m/px.

blurb: A real 12 deg rim grade over 184 m of relief, from LOLA polar topography at 5 m/px — the finest terrain in this set. WorldVLA pushes as if it were on the flat and its own metrics show the cost: 0.67 m of pelvis bounce, 22.9 deg of peak pitch, four recoveries and two missed contacts. PragyaSpace takes short controlled steps and keeps the mass over the feet.
